reading.body:
Privacy and AI hiring in this sample is mostly legal and governance work at AI vendors, not engineering: four of five postings are counsel, advisor, or program roles.

The five postings were listed between July 14 and September 11, 2026, and collected on September 12. Harvey posted one title, Privacy and AI Counsel EMEA, twice, once for London and once for Dublin. OpenAI's opening is a research engineer for privacy. Figure's is a technical program manager for security and privacy. The locations are München, London, Dublin, San Francisco, and San Jose. Three of the five are flagged remote.

The pattern is a compliance layer forming around deployed AI rather than around the machines that run it. Counsel and governance roles scale with the number of jurisdictions a vendor sells into, which is why one employer lists two European cities under a single title. The one engineering role sits closer to the model itself, where privacy work touches training data and evaluation. None of this measures compute, buildings, or power, and it should not be read as doing so.

Five postings is a snapshot, not a rate. The data carries no salary, seniority, or comparison against other job functions, so it cannot show whether privacy hiring is growing or shrinking. Coverage is uneven because the underlying sources mix aggregators with direct company boards, and employers that do not post publicly will not appear at all. What the sample does show is where the demand sits: European legal markets and United States AI employers.
